speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are experiencing persistent vomiting and chest pain; these can be signs of several conditions, including gallstones, pancreatitis, or a cardiac issue. To begin, have you noticed if the pain radiates to your back, jaw, or left arm, and does it worsen after eating or lying down? Also, please tell me if you have a history of gallbladder disease or recent heavy alcohol consumption.

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave syndrome (spontaneous esophageal rupture).

Based on your history of forceful vomiting after heavy alcohol consumption followed by severe chest pain and coughing, this is highly suspicious for an esophageal rupture. This is a medical emergency requiring immediate imaging; REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_CXR (upright and left lateral decubitus).
